newsitem.title: UK: UK's Referendum Party launches cinema ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: UK's Referendum Party launches cinema ad campaign.

text.p: Britain's Referendum Party is breaking out the political popcorn with the launch on Friday of a seven-week cinema advertising campaign.

It is only the second time that a British political party has advertised in cinemas, a Referendum Party spokesman said. The first political advertising shown in cinemas was done by the Labour Party in 1987.
The Referendum Party's campaign includes two ads being shown in 750 cinemas throughout the UK. The party said the ads are expected to reach an audience of 7.5 million people.
"Our message is humourous, it's quite stylish," the party spokesman told Reuters.

One 50-second ad is based on the theme of the bulldog biting back. The other ad runs 30 seconds and "...is based on power being pulled away from 10 Downing Street, so it doesn't matter who you vote for," the spokesman said.
Sir James Goldsmith, the billionaire financier who founded the party, does not appear in either advert.

Cinema advertising was targeted because cinema audiences tend to be youthful and because cinemas offer a leisure setting with a receptive audience, the Referendum Party spokesman said. He declined to disclose the cost of the ad campaign, but said, "We're running a campaign that matches the other political parties."

The Referendum Party, which claims British sovereignty is being seriously eroded by the growing power of the European Union, is calling for a referendum on the UK's relations with the EU. The party plans to contest all the seats at Britain's upcoming general election, except those where the candidate of one of the main parties has come out for a referendum on the European Union.
The Referendum Party has a war chest of 20 million sterling to finance its political efforts.
